problem_text:
A logistics firm must devise a procurement and stock management scheme for a critical spare part across a 7-week operational window.
The initial stockpile at the outset of the planning interval is 45 units.
In each week t = 1, ..., 7, the supplier permits the firm to issue a procurement request whose volume must fall between 13 and 22 units.
Nevertheless, every procurement request dispatched will require a lead time of 4 week(s) before it becomes available for fulfilling requirements or rebuilding the stockpile.
The requirement for the spare part in each week is specified as follows:
* Week 1: requirement 41 units
* Week 2: requirement 48 units
* Week 3: requirement 55 units
* Week 4: requirement 15 units
* Week 5: requirement 53 units
* Week 6: requirement 54 units
* Week 7: requirement 19 units

Stockouts are tolerated, but any unfilled requirement will be entirely forfeited and not carried forward.
Throughout the planning window, part quantities may assume fractional values, and the aggregate volume of physical stock on the premises at any moment must not surpass the storage facility's limit of 45 units.

In week 4, the maximum procurement volume is restricted to 15 units.
In week 1, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 2 units.

The aggregate expenditure over the planning window comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 4 per unit procured; the storage expense, which amounts to 2 per unit of stock held over from one week to the next; and the stockout penalty, which amounts to 13 per unit of unfulfilled requirement. Ascertain the optimal procurement volume for each week and monitor the consequent stock and stockout levels in order to minimize the total expenditure.
